authority: Reference-project design authority delegated by the user: Take the best decisions as the owner and complete the implementation.
scope: Decisions for this reference implementation, not an assertion of upstream API-owner approval or production/sandbox certification.

decisions.title: Account.name
decisions.choice: Optional; accept the published account examples. STRICT_ACCOUNT_NAME is an explicit opt-in interoperability profile.
decisions.rationale: Avoid rejecting valid documented account shapes because of an undefined required property.

decisions.title: Refresh token lifecycle
decisions.choice: Reusable refresh tokens, 30-day configurable lifetime, 10-minute access tokens; code reuse revokes its issued family. No rotation field in refresh responses.
decisions.rationale: Keep the declared response shape and do not assume Uber persists replacement refresh tokens.

decisions.title: HTTP errors
decisions.choice: Unexpected/transient errors return retryable500 on every route, empty when undeclared, and are never cached. Authentication uses declared401, otherwise the existing declared400 mapping.
decisions.rationale: Never misclassify infrastructure failures as final validation errors; minimize unnecessary wire-contract changes.

decisions.title: Cancelled lookup
decisions.choice: Return200 with status CANCELLED for cancelled or expired authorizations. Add this value explicitly to the derived reference runtime schema, not the unchanged upstream pin.
decisions.rationale: A successful lookup should describe a known terminal business state rather than return a validation error. This is a visible additive reference-contract extension.

decisions.title: Partial capture
decisions.choice: Allow one positive capture up to the authorization. Successful partial capture closes it and releases all unused hold; preserve authorized_e5 and store amount_e5 as actually captured. Refunds are capped at captured funds; another capture conflicts409.
decisions.rationale: Support a useful payment lifecycle without ambiguous multi-capture accounting or indefinitely retained residual holds.

decisions.title: Capture decline
decisions.choice: Return422 with BANK_HARD_ERROR/BANK_SOFT_ERROR. A definitive rejected capture does not debit and releases the entire original authorization, including a partial-capture attempt. Unknown transport outcomes remain retryable500/reconciliation.
decisions.rationale: Follow the declared error response and distinguish a known business rejection from an uncertain processor effect.

decisions.title: Cancel response
decisions.rationale: Follow the declared response schema; do not invent a response body.

decisions.title: Lookup identity
decisions.choice: Use Uber transaction/refund ID; merchant_reference, if supplied, must match.
decisions.rationale: Follow parameter definitions and keep Uber identity separate from PSP reference.

decisions.title: Rejected callback reference
decisions.choice: Always include an immutable PSP reference, including rejection.
decisions.rationale: Satisfy the required schema and make reconciliation unambiguous.

decisions.title: Authorization-code result
decisions.choice: Code exchange returns refresh token; obtain access token using the refresh grant.
decisions.rationale: Follow grant-specific schemas rather than conflicting sequence diagrams.

decisions.title: Deposit callback routing
decisions.choice: Only an explicitly configured asynchronous charge funding profile with callback_mode=deposit uses confirm/cancel/updateDeposit. Ordinary charge uses chargeCallback; refund and payout keep their own callbacks. Amount may only decrease before confirmation; queue update before confirm.
decisions.rationale: No heuristic routing by transaction ID or funding-code string. Preserve clear flow boundaries and never increase a user-approved hold without new authorization.

decisions.title: Balance request
decisions.choice: Use account_id and funding_method, with scoped account-bound bearer plus signature.
decisions.rationale: Follow the actual operation schema and preserve ownership checks.

decisions.title: Refund wire contract
decisions.choice: Use original_transaction_id, original_merchant_reference and CurrencyAmount. Return201 CONFIRMED/PENDING/REJECTED. Ordered late rejection reverses a confirmed refund once; unrecovered funds become explicit debt without consuming other holds.
decisions.rationale: Follow schemas; implement a durable, auditable local reversal policy rather than contradictory SUCCEEDED/FAILED examples.

decisions.title: Payout identity conflict
decisions.choice: Changed payload under the same payout ID or key returns409 DUPLICATE_REQUEST_ERROR; identical payload replays.
decisions.rationale: Use the declared conflict response and never repeat a payout effect to resolve a key conflict.

decisions.title: Reference settlement
decisions.choice: Closed UTC periods, daily by default; immutable confirmation/reversal journal; one canonical JSONL file per source account with monetary entries (an empty period has an empty manifest) and a checksummed manifest; decimal-string signed E5 and per-currency totals. Seal once, reject overlaps, replay bytes. Atomic directory or strict-host-key local SFTP publication occurs outside SQL; transport receipt is not financial acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Provide a complete runnable reconciliation workflow without claiming the chosen format is an Uber bilateral format or fabricating real hosts, keys, schedules, commercial netting or acceptance.
